title: Suspicious service creation with encoded PowerShell on WORKSTATION6
summary: At 06:57 on 2020-09-20, a newly created service named PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX on WORKSTATION6 launched an encoded PowerShell command shell seconds after user pgustuvo logged in from 172.18.39.5. The encoded command attempted to disable script block logging and AMSI, then download and execute code from http://10.10.10.5. The user typically works from WORKSTATION5, making this location anomaly suspicious. All evidence points to a coordinated attack involving remote service execution, persistence via new service, and defense evasion.
evidence: New service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX installed on WORKSTATION6 under user pgustavo
Service command line uses PowerShell with -enc flag to bypass security controls
Decoded command attempts to disable ScriptBlockLogging and bypass AMSI
Command contacts external IP 10.10.10.5 for download of additional payload
User pgustavo normally logs in from WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
Service created seconds after network logon from 172.18.39.5
Rule tags T1021.002, T1543.003, T1569.002 confirm remote service execution, service creation, and service execution techniques

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 immediately from network to prevent lateral movement and further payload execution
Terminate the malicious service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and investigate for credential compromise
Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at the perimeter firewall
Review all services and scheduled tasks on WORKSTATION6 for additional persistence mechanisms
Audit pgustavo's logon history and session activity on WORKSTATION5 and WORKSTATION6
Enable enhanced monitoring for encoded PowerShell commands and service creation events across the environment

This follows prior true positive ALERT-001 on same host.

Decoded command disables Script Block Logging and bypasses AMSI antivirus scanning
Downloads from IP 10.10.10.5 which is suspicious: private address not in company known network ranges
Contains nested base64 encoding and proxy credential usage
Follows prior true positive ALERT-001 for suspicious service creation on same host
related_to_prior: ALERT-001 (true_positive) on WORKSTATION6 - likely attack chain continuation

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Block IP 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy level

title: C2 Beacon via Encoded PowerShell on WORKSTATION6
summary: On WORKSTATION6, SYSTEM user launched an encoded PowerShell command (-enc) that connected to external IP 10.10.10.5:80. The decoded command disables script block logging, bypasses AMSI, and downloads/runs remote code — classic C2 beacon behavior. The destination IP is suspicious: private address but not in company network ranges. This is part of an ongoing attack chain following ALERT-001 and ALERT-002 on the same host.
evidence: powershell.exe as SYSTEM connected to 10.10.10.5:80 (1 connection)
Encoded command decoded: disables script block logging, bypasses AMSI, downloads from web, runs downloaded code
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious — private address but not in company known ranges
Process chain: services.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe → whoami.exe
Decoded preview shows: IF $PSVersion >= 3 then disable ScriptBlockLogging and EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging
Prior alerts ALERT-001 and ALERT-002 on WORKSTATION6 were true positives, confirming attack chain
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain on WORKSTATION6: ALERT-001 (suspicious service creation) → ALERT-002 (encoded PowerShell disabling security controls) → ALERT-003 (C2 beacon communication)

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Terminate active powershell and whoami processes on WORKSTATION6
Block outbound traffic to 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Full malware scan and forensic image of WORKSTATION6
Review all other hosts for similar encoded PowerShell patterns and connections to 10.10.10.5
Audit and restore any Group Policy settings modified by the script (ScriptBlockLogging)

title: Azure Guest Agent legitimate lsass memory access during log collection
summary: On WORKSTATION5, the legitimate Azure Guest Agent (CollectGuestLogs.exe) opened lsass.exe during normal log collection operations. The process was initiated by WaAppAgent.exe as SYSTEM user with command line "CollectGuestLogs.exe -Mode:ga -FileName:...", indicating it's performing authorized Azure guest log collection. Multiple opens of lsass with read access (0x1000) are consistent with this legitimate function. The alert's 0x1410 access at 06:58:01 falls within this normal activity pattern.
evidence: CollectGuestLogs.exe is a legitimate Azure Guest Agent component (Microsoft signed/verified)
Process started by WaAppAgent.exe as USER SYSTEM with command line "-Mode:ga -FileName:..." indicating authorized log collection
Multiple lsass open events with 0x1000 access are part of normal Guest Agent log gathering
The specific 0x1410 access at alert time is consistent with the pattern of other lsass accesses
Command line parameters -Mode:ga and -FileName confirm this is log collection, not credential dumping
IP reputation check showed 10.0.0.1 is private address not in company network (irrelevant but confirmed)
related_to_prior: N/A - this is an isolated false positive alert; prior alerts (ALERT-001 to ALERT-003) involved genuine attacks on WORKSTATION6 with encoded PowerShell, unrelated to this Azure Agent activity on WORKSTATION5

recommended_actions.action: Close alert - no action required, this is legitimate Azure Guest Agent behavior
If concerned, verify Azure Guest Agent version and ensure LSA Protection/Credential Guard is enabled on the host
